subtitulo: Ferragosto empties the cities, the patron saint's day closes one town and not the next, and the sagra is the best meal of your trip
cena: It is the middle of August, the street you liked is entirely shuttered, and a handwritten sign says something about the twenty-second.
frasePiso: Ask what is on this week before you plan it. The closures are findable and so are the festivals, and one of them is why you came.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Ferragosto, 15 August, is a national public holiday and the peak of the Italian summer break, when many small businesses in cities close for a period around it. In addition, each comune observes its own patron saint's day as a local public holiday — Rome on 29 June, Milan on 7 December, Naples on 19 September, Venice on 25 April — so a town can be closed while the one next to it is fully open.
fatosDatados.fonte: Governo Italiano — calendario delle festività nazionali; regolamenti comunali sui santi patroni

steps.pt: Italy has two calendars. The national one you can look up, and the local one that closes a town without warning.
The big one is Ferragosto, the fifteenth of August. Cities empty, shops shut, and the coast fills up.

steps.acao: Read the reopening date on the sign. Plan the week around it instead of returning tomorrow.
steps.es: Chiuso per ferie dal dieci al venticinque agosto.
steps.pt: Closed for holidays from the tenth to the twenty-fifth of August.
steps.tts: Chiuso per ferie dal dieci al venticinque agosto.

steps.pt: August in a city is not a failed trip. It is a different one: emptier, hotter, with the coast doing the living.

steps.promptPt: Ask what is closed this week before you build a plan. Speak now.

steps.pt: The second calendar is the patron saint. Every town has its own day off, and the next town has another.

steps.acao: That is a local holiday, not a national one. The next town over will be working normally.
steps.es: Domani è il santo patrono, è festa solo qui.
steps.pt: Tomorrow is the patron saint's day, it's a holiday only here.
steps.tts: Domani è il santo patrono, è festa solo qui.

steps.promptPt: Ask when the patron saint's day is here. Speak now.
steps.pt: When is the patron saint's day here?
And the third thing, worth moving a trip for: the sagra. A village festival built around one ingredient.

steps.acao: Go. Long tables, one dish, cash only, and better than any restaurant that week.
steps.es: Sabato c'è la sagra del cinghiale, al campo sportivo.
steps.pt: Saturday there's the wild boar festival, at the sports ground.
steps.tts: Sabato c'è la sagra del cinghiale, al campo sportivo.

steps.promptPt: Ask whether there is a sagra nearby this weekend. Speak now.
steps.es: C'è qualche sagra qui vicino nel weekend?
steps.pinyin: cheh KWAL-keh SA-gra kwee vee-CHEE-no nel week-END
steps.pt: Is there a sagra nearby at the weekend?
steps.tts: C'è qualche sagra qui vicino nel weekend?

steps.promptPt: Ask the practical question — whether you need cash. Speak now.
steps.es: Si paga in contanti alla sagra?
steps.pinyin: see PA-ga een kon-TAN-tee AL-la SA-gra
steps.pt: Do you pay in cash at the sagra?
steps.tts: Si paga in contanti alla sagra?

steps.acao: Bring cash. This is the one place where the card rule genuinely does not help you.
steps.es: Sì, contanti. Prendi i buoni alla cassa all'ingresso.
steps.pt: Yes, cash. You get the tickets at the till by the entrance.
steps.tts: Sì, contanti. Prendi i buoni alla cassa all'ingresso.

steps.promptPt: Ask what time the festival starts. Speak now.
steps.es: A che ora comincia la sagra?
steps.pinyin: a keh O-ra ko-MEEN-cha la SA-gra
steps.pt: What time does the sagra start?
steps.tts: A che ora comincia la sagra?

steps.promptPt: Ask whether the shops reopen before you leave. Speak now.

steps.pt: A06 done. Ferragosto empties the cities, the saint closes one town only, and the sagra is worth rearranging for.

secoes.corpo: The fifteenth of August, a national holiday and the centre of the summer break. Many small businesses close for a stretch around it, cities thin out and the coast fills. It is entirely visible in advance and catches visitors anyway.

exemplos.pt: When is the patron saint's day here?

secoes.corpo: Each comune has its own saint's day as a public holiday, so closures can be town-specific. Rome, Milan, Naples and Venice all have different dates, and a day trip can land on one of them without warning.

secoes.titulo: The sagra is the best meal you will not have planned
secoes.corpo: A village festival built around one ingredient — porcini, wild boar, chestnut, a particular pasta — cooked in volume by people from the village, served at long tables. It is usually cash, usually a ticket system, and usually the food you will remember.

Sagre are advertised on paper: posters on walls, banners over roads, a sign at the roundabout. They are frequently invisible online and completely visible from the street, which is why the question in this part is asked of a person rather than a phone.

permissao: You are allowed to rearrange a trip around a village festival you found out about from a poster. Skipping a booked museum for a sagra is not a wasted day — it is the choice that separates the trip you planned from the one you will actually talk about.
espelho: Anyone who has arrived somewhere on a public holiday they did not know existed knows the flat feeling of a closed street. The fix is the same everywhere — ask a local before you plan the week, not after.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You take a day trip to a nearby town and find everything shut, though your own town was open and busy that morning.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: I got the opening hours wrong, or something has happened.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Each comune keeps its patron saint's day as a local public holiday, and the dates differ from town to town. A closure twenty minutes down the road can be a full holiday there and an ordinary Tuesday where you slept.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Ask quand'è il santo patrono qui? about anywhere you plan to visit, and check it the day before rather than on arrival.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You either avoid the closed day or, better, arrive on it deliberately — the saint's day usually comes with a procession, a market and the town at its most itself.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not for large chains, supermarkets and transport, which mostly run normally, and not in the biggest tourist centres where the local holiday barely dents commercial hours.
